question: Minimize the total operational costs, which include production setup costs, machine startup costs, inventory holding costs, and backlogging costs, while meeting customer demand for each product in each period. The decisions involve determining whether to produce each product on each machine in each period, deciding whether to start up each machine for each product in each period, determining the exact quantity of each product to produce on each machine in each period, and deciding how much inventory to carry over or how much demand to backlog for each product in each period. The total cost includes production setup costs of 149.1695690337089 per production run, machine startup costs of 69.24269269143792 per machine startup, inventory holding costs of 1.080318154052025 for Product 0 and 1.143069947055348 for Product 1, and backlogging costs of 6.798895023015501 for Product 0 and 6.372651501311341 for Product 1. The constraints ensure that the total production of each product across all machines, plus any inventory carried over from the previous period, minus any backlog from the previous period, equals the demand for that product in the current period, plus any inventory carried forward, minus any backlogged demand. The demands are 22.92965094851524 units for Product 0 in Period 0, 19.03396834281949 units in Period 1, and 18.90167422155575 units in Period 2, and 19.80185049682801 units for Product 1 in Period 0, 24.22810173621122 units in Period 1, and 16.84556169689551 units in Period 2. The production quantity on each machine, plus the startup time, cannot exceed the machine's capacity, which is 76.7045484622153 for Machine 0 and 69.3695364951939 for Machine 1. Each machine can only produce one product at a time in any given period. If a machine is used for production in a period but was not used in the previous period, a startup cost is incurred. Production quantities, inventory levels, and backlogs must be non-negative, and production and startup decisions must be binary.

def build_model(data=None):

    m = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    m.P = pyo.Set(initialize=d["products"], ordered=True)
    m.M = pyo.Set(initialize=d["machines"], ordered=True)
    m.T = pyo.Set(initialize=d["periods"], ordered=True)

    # Production quantity
    m.x = pyo.Var(m.P, m.M, m.T, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # Production / setup indicator
    m.y = pyo.Var(m.P, m.M, m.T, within=pyo.Binary)

    # Machine startup for a product
    m.z = pyo.Var(m.P, m.M, m.T, within=pyo.Binary)

    # Inventory carried forward (out of the period it is indexed by)
    m.I = pyo.Var(m.P, m.T, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    # Backlog accumulating at the end of the period it is indexed by
    m.B = pyo.Var(m.P, m.T, within=pyo.NonNegativeReals)

    def obj_rule(mm):
        setup = sum(d["setup_cost"] * mm.y[p, k, t]
                    for p in mm.P for k in mm.M for t in mm.T)
        startup = sum(d["startup_cost"] * mm.z[p, k, t]
                      for p in mm.P for k in mm.M for t in mm.T)
        holding = sum(d["holding_cost"][p] * mm.I[p, t]
                      for p in mm.P for t in mm.T)
        backlog = sum(d["backlog_cost"][p] * mm.B[p, t]
                      for p in mm.P for t in mm.T)
        return setup + startup + holding + backlog

    m.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # --- Inventory balance per product and period ---
    def balance_rule(mm, p, t):
        tset = list(mm.T)
        idx = tset.index(t)
        inv_in = mm.I[p, tset[idx - 1]] if idx > 0 else 0.0
        back_in = mm.B[p, tset[idx - 1]] if idx > 0 else 0.0
        return (sum(mm.x[p, k, t] for k in mm.M) + inv_in + mm.B[p, t]
                == d["demand"][p][t] + mm.I[p, t] + back_in)

    m.balance = pyo.Constraint(m.P, m.T, rule=balance_rule)

    # --- Capacity: production + startup time <= machine capacity ---
    def capacity_rule(mm, p, k, t):
        return mm.x[p, k, t] + d["startup_time"] * mm.z[p, k, t] <= d["capacity"][k]

    m.capacity = pyo.Constraint(m.P, m.M, m.T, rule=capacity_rule)

    # --- Production only when set-up / run indicator is on (big-M) ---
    def setup_link_rule(mm, p, k, t):
        return mm.x[p, k, t] <= d["big_m"] * mm.y[p, k, t]

    m.setup_link = pyo.Constraint(m.P, m.M, m.T, rule=setup_link_rule)

    # --- Startup indicator is on only when the run indicator is on ---
    def startup_link_rule(mm, p, k, t):
        return mm.z[p, k, t] <= mm.y[p, k, t]

    m.startup_link = pyo.Constraint(m.P, m.M, m.T, rule=startup_link_rule)

    # --- One product per machine per period ---
    def one_product_rule(mm, k, t):
        return sum(mm.y[p, k, t] for p in mm.P) <= 1

    m.one_product = pyo.Constraint(m.M, m.T, rule=one_product_rule)

    # --- Startup logic for period 0: used implies started ---
    def startup_first_rule(mm, p, k):
        t0 = list(mm.T)[0]
        return mm.z[p, k, t0] >= mm.y[p, k, t0]

    m.startup_first = pyo.Constraint(m.P, m.M, rule=startup_first_rule)

    # --- Startup logic for later periods: used now and not before implies started ---
    def startup_logic_rule(mm, p, k, t):
        tset = list(mm.T)
        idx = tset.index(t)
        if idx == 0:
            return pyo.Constraint.Skip
        tprev = tset[idx - 1]
        return mm.z[p, k, t] >= mm.y[p, k, t] - mm.y[p, k, tprev]

    m.startup_logic = pyo.Constraint(m.P, m.M, m.T, rule=startup_logic_rule)

    return m

    # Decision variables
    model.produce = pyo.Var(model.P, model.M, model.T,
                            domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    model.setup = pyo.Var(model.P, model.M, model.T,
                          domain=pyo.Binary)
    model.startup = pyo.Var(model.P, model.M, model.T,
                            domain=pyo.Binary)
    model.inventory = pyo.Var(model.P, model.T,
                              domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    model.backlog = pyo.Var(model.P, model.T,
                            domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    model.machine_used = pyo.Var(model.M, model.T,
                                 domain=pyo.Binary)

    # Objective: minimize total operational cost
    def obj_rule(m):
        setup_term = sum(d["setup_cost"] * m.setup[p, k, t]
                         for p in m.P for k in m.M for t in m.T)
        startup_term = sum(d["startup_cost"] * m.startup[p, k, t]
                           for p in m.P for k in m.M for t in m.T)
        hold_term = sum(d["holding_cost"][p] * m.inventory[p, t]
                        for p in m.P for t in m.T)
        back_term = sum(d["backlog_cost"][p] * m.backlog[p, t]
                        for p in m.P for t in m.T)
        return setup_term + startup_term + hold_term + back_term

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Inventory balance for each product and period
    def balance_rule(m, p, t):
        prev_inv = m.inventory[p, t - 1] if t - 1 in m.T else 0.0
        prev_back = m.backlog[p, t - 1] if t - 1 in m.T else 0.0
        total_prod = sum(m.produce[p, k, t] for k in m.M)
        return (total_prod + prev_inv - prev_back
                == d["demand"][(p, t)] + m.inventory[p, t] - m.backlog[p, t])

    model.balance = pyo.Constraint(model.P, model.T, rule=balance_rule)

    # Capacity: production + startup time <= machine capacity
    def capacity_rule(m, k, t):
        total_prod = sum(m.produce[p, k, t] for p in m.P)
        total_startup = sum(m.startup[p, k, t] for p in m.P)
        return total_prod + d["startup_time"] * total_startup <= d["machine_capacity"][k]

    model.capacity = pyo.Constraint(model.M, model.T, rule=capacity_rule)

    # Link production to setup (big-M)
    def setup_link_rule(m, p, k, t):
        return m.produce[p, k, t] <= d["big_m"] * m.setup[p, k, t]

    model.setup_link = pyo.Constraint(model.P, model.M, model.T, rule=setup_link_rule)

    # One product at a time per machine per period
    def one_product_rule(m, k, t):
        return sum(m.setup[p, k, t] for p in m.P) <= 1

    model.one_product = pyo.Constraint(model.M, model.T, rule=one_product_rule)

    # Machine used if any product is set up on it
    def machine_used_rule(m, k, t):
        return m.machine_used[k, t] == sum(m.setup[p, k, t] for p in m.P)

    model.machine_used_con = pyo.Constraint(model.M, model.T, rule=machine_used_rule)

    # Startup logic: startup >= machine_used[t] - machine_used[t-1]
    def startup_rule(m, p, k, t):
        prev_used = m.machine_used[k, t - 1] if t - 1 in m.T else 0.0
        return m.startup[p, k, t] >= m.setup[p, k, t] - prev_used

    model.startup_con = pyo.Constraint(model.P, model.M, model.T, rule=startup_rule)

    # Startup only when product is set up
    def startup_link_rule(m, p, k, t):
        return m.startup[p, k, t] <= m.setup[p, k, t]

    model.startup_link = pyo.Constraint(model.P, model.M, model.T, rule=startup_link_rule)

    return model

    #         = demand[p,t] + inv[p,t] - back[p,t]
    def balance_rule(m, p, t):
        prev_inv = m.inv[p, t - 1] if t - 1 in m.T else 0.0
        prev_back = m.back[p, t - 1] if t - 1 in m.T else 0.0
        produced = sum(m.prod[mm, p, t] for mm in m.M)
        return (produced + prev_inv - prev_back
                == d["demand"][(p, t)] + m.inv[p, t] - m.back[p, t])

    m.balance = pyo.Constraint(m.P, m.T, rule=balance_rule)

    # (2) Capacity: production quantity plus startup time cannot exceed capacity.
    #     prod[m,p,t] <= capacity[m] * setup[m,p,t]
    def capacity_rule(m, mm, p, t):
        return m.prod[mm, p, t] <= d["capacity"][mm] * m.setup[mm, p, t]

    m.capacity = pyo.Constraint(m.M, m.P, m.T, rule=capacity_rule)

    # (3) Each machine produces at most one product per period.
    def one_product_rule(m, mm, t):
        return sum(m.setup[mm, p, t] for p in m.P) <= 1

    m.one_product = pyo.Constraint(m.M, m.T, rule=one_product_rule)

    # (4) Startup linking: start[m,p,t] >= setup[m,p,t] - setup[m,p,t-1]
    #     (startup incurred when machine used for product p in t but not in t-1)
    def startup_rule(m, mm, p, t):
        prev = m.setup[mm, p, t - 1] if t - 1 in m.T else 0.0
        return m.start[mm, p, t] >= m.setup[mm, p, t] - prev

    m.startup = pyo.Constraint(m.M, m.P, m.T, rule=startup_rule)

    return m
